These cold-blooded lizard-like people have lived here for centuries, and instead of embracing technological progress, they chose industrial reliability. They are not afraid to utilise their military might to bring peace and order in the surrounding lands.\n\nOriginally engineered to survive on not-fully-terraformed planets with no humidity what-so-ever, saurids are a closely knit community that prefers to treat outsiders with aggression and show of force.
Carriers of this gene have lizard-like frilled ears.

Carriers of this gene grow a short, scaly tail that has no function what-so-ever.
Carriers of this gene have hands that partially resemble dinosaur claws. This has a slight impact on their ability to manipulate objects, but allows them to deal deep cuts in melee combat.
Carriers of this gene lay eggs instead of giving live birth. Eggs need time and correct conditions to hatch.
Carriers of this gene need to maintain a steady body temperature. Being too hot or too cold will result in loss of motor functions, and if unchecked too long - death.
Carriers of this gene excrete special pheromones that attract members of the same xenotype.
Carriers of this gene grow scales all over their body, which protect them from sharp damage of any kind.
Carriers have a terrifying voice like that of a dinosaur.

Genetically spliced with synthesized reptile genetic material for improved compatibility with arid environments, saurids are cold-blooded isolationists with harsh voices and extremely low metabolisms. Their sharp claws and hardened scales make them particularly suited to melee encounters.\n\nFor workers looking for higher-wage jobs, saurid xenogerms are offered alongside employment packages to particularly arid and hot planets. As conditions are quite harsh, they experience an attitude shift to be less social and consume fewer calories which allows them to be more profitable. As they are not excluded from starting families, saurids can communicate with each other using pheromones and are oviparous to reduce medical complications caused by lack of proper social infrastructure.

Genetically engineered to survive on extremely low nutrition in the most arid environments, saurids adapt very well to hostile environments thanks to the oviparous nature of their reproduction as well as lizard-like genetic features. They prefer isolation and prefer to mate with other saurids.

After laying an egg, it is common with those with the oviparous gene to go through a short period of sterility till they are capable of producing another. This is only a temporary condition and causes no long term effects.
